QANTAS
AIRBUS
A380-800
SAFETY INSTRUCTIONS
Additional safety information
Obey the authority of the crew
All passengers must follow, without question, any
lawful direction(s) given by any member of the
crew. The Captain is responsible for the
maintenance of discipline by all persons on board.
You must not obstruct or impede any crew member
from exercising a power, or performing a duty,
under the Civil Aviation legislation.
Fasten your seat belt for take-off
You must keep your seat belt fastened during
take-off, landing and whenever the fasten seat belt
sign is on. Make sure that it is low and tight over
your hips. Familiarise yourself with how to fasten
and unfasten it. While seated keep your seat belt
on. It will assist to protect you from injury. Tighten
your seat belt again before landing. On arrival,
remain in your seat with your seat belt fastened
until the seat belt sign is turned off.
Smoking is not permitted
Under Australian Government Regulations smoking
is not allowed on any Qantas aircraft. Fire is one of
the greatest dangers to an aircraft. Smoking especially
in the toilet, creates a serious fire hazard. Smoke
detectors have been fitted in every toilet for your
safety. Heavy penalties apply for non compliance
with non-smoking regulations.
Keep seatbacks upright for take-off
and landing
For all take-off and landings seatbacks must be in
the upright position with tray tables stowed away.
In an evacuation - leave your carry on
baggage onboard
Taking your carry on baggage in an emergency
will slow your progress and may cause injury to
yourself or others on the escape slide. The time
spent retrieving items may prevent you or
someone else, from escaping. It is best to carry
your passport and essential medicines on your
person. Remember, the number one priority is
- Evacuate as quickly as possible. Locate your
nearest emergency exits. Knowing the location of
your nearest emergency exits will ensure valuable
time is not lost during an emergency evacuation.
Locate your closest exit row and an alternative in
case the first is unavailable. Count the number of
seat rows between you and these exits. This will
assist you if your vision is restricted in a darkened
or smoke filled cabin. Interior emergency lighting
will guide you to the emergency exits. The escape
path, and exit lighting will automatically illuminate
in an emergency. Always listen to the instructions
of the crew who are trained to recognise if the
exit is safe to open.
Know the 'brace' position for impact
Assuming the 'BRACE' position in the event
of an accident will reduce impact forces on your
body and reduces injuries. 'BRACE' positions are
shown on the front of this card. Know which is
most suitable for you in the seat in which you are
sitting. If the crew shout "BRACE, BRACE, BRACE,
heads down, stay down" adopt the 'BRACE'
position until the aircraft stops completely then
listen for the crews' instructions. Remember there
could be more than one impact.
reached the ground, immediately move away from
the aircraft. Move away quickly in the opposite
direction of any smoke or fire. Do not smoke or use
electronic devices until advised it is safe to do so.
Jump and sit onto the evacuation slide
Inflatable escape slides are found at all doors.
See the diagram in the centre section of this card
which shows the exits on this aircraft. When using
an escape slide, remove high heels. Jump on to the
slide and then sit with your feet and legs together.
Place your hands on your knees. Do not use your
arms/hands to slow you down as this could result
in injury from painful slide burns. Once you have
What are Dangerous Goods?
Dangerous Goods are items that may endanger
the safety of an aircraft or persons on board the
aircraft. Dangerous Goods are also known as
restricted articles, hazardous materials and
dangerous cargo. Their carriage on Qantas aircraft
is primarily governed by the Civil Aviation Safety
Authority Regulations. Dangerous Goods must not
be carried in (or as) passenger or crew-checked
baggage or carry-on baggage. Security type attache
cases incorporating Dangerous Goods, such as
lithium batteries or pyrotechnic devices, are totally
forbidden. Disabling devices such as mace, pepper
spray, etc. containing an irritant or incapacitating
substance are prohibited on the person, in checked
and carry-on baggage.
RESTRICTIONS ON THE USE OF ELECTRONIC DEVICES Some electronic devices may affect the
operation of the aircraft instruments and systems, therefore all electronic devices including mobile
phones, Personal Digital Assistants (PDA's), lap top computers, handheld games and toys must be
switched off before take-off and landing. Please observe the following restrictions listed below.
Devices prohibited for use at all
times whilst the aircraft is in flight.
Radio receivers or transmitters, two way radios (walkie talkies), devices
with WiMax technology, pagers, radio/remote controlled toys/devices,
mobile phones without Flight Mode/Flight Safe capability and any
other electronic devices not mentioned.
Devices that are permitted for use
in flight after take-off when the
seatbelt sign has extinguished,
until commencement of descent.
Personal computers with inbuilt WiFi or Blue Tooth access devices.
PDA's (without mobile phones) electronic games, personal music
devices such as compact disc, mini disc, MP3, AM/FM radios (receive
only) and one way pagers.
Devices that are permitted for use
in flight with FLIGHT MODE/FLIGHT
SAFE capability after takeoff when
the seatbelt sign has extinguished,
until commencement of descent.
Mobile/Cellular phones, PDA's and computers with inbuilt devices
using the Global System for Mobile Communications (GS) including
3G and GRPS technologies or the Advanced Mobile Phone System
(AMPS) as a communication technique
Note: The non - transmitting capability ("flight mode" or "flight safe")
must be selected prior to the device being switched off before takeoff,
to ensure that the device is unable to transmit during flight.
Devices not restricted from use.
Devices that are required for the essential support of human
life such as medical implants, other medical devices that have prior
approval by Qantas. Global Positioning Receivers (GPS), electric
shavers, video and still cameras which are electronically powered,
pocket calculators, other devices powered by micro-cell batteries
and solar cells.
Note: No person may use Personal Electronic Devices (PED's) that can adversely effect the safe operation of an aircraft. Due to
increasing advances in PED technology, please consult the Qantas Australian Way magazine for further information regarding
suitability. If the customer is unable to demonstrate to Cabin Crew that the transmitting capability of the Portable Electronic
Device (PED) is switched off, the device must be turned off and stowed appropriately. Should an extended ground delay be
encountered, at the Captain's direction only, mobile phones may be used.
PLEASE DO NOT REMOVE THIS CARD FROM THE AIRCRAFT
